stem: Eklavya converts $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to Fahrenheit. He also converts a length of $4\,\mathrm{m}$ to centimetres.

parts.text: Which claim matches each kind of measurement to the correct conversion relation?

options.text: Temperature uses $F=\frac{9}{5}C+32$, so $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}=77^{\circ}\mathrm{F}$; length uses $1\,\mathrm{m}=100\,\mathrm{cm}$, so $4\,\mathrm{m}=400\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Call the answer the phrase target unit alone, and stop.
Convert $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ by multiplying by $100$, because $100$ is the standout factor printed near the length conversion.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Celsius–Fahrenheit needs the offset formula F=(9/5)C+32, while metre–centimetre uses the length equivalence 1 m=100 cm. Mixing those relations fails the hinge.

teacher.key_rationale: F=(9/5)*25+32=77 and 4 m=400 cm. Naming target unit alone or borrowing the length factor 100 for temperature both miss matching the conversion to the kind of measurement.
